summary: Croatia's Interior Ministry publishes victims and perpetrators of every Criminal Code article, including child sexual abuse, child pornography and violation of a child's rights, with a count of foreign citizens, and the statistics bureau publishes convictions by citizenship. That is a citizenship proxy on both sides; no ethnicity or national minority is recorded in crime data.

nations.National (Interior Ministry, DZS): Annual police statistical review; court-based conviction tables.

european_title: Not recorded by any Croatian crime source
european_note: Croatian crime statistics separate only foreign citizens from Croatian citizens. National minorities (Serbs, Roma and others) are counted in the census but not in any crime, victim or child-protection statistic, so neither ethnic Europeans nor any ethnic group can be measured for child harm.
proxy_note: Croatia records citizenship only in crime data, never ethnicity or national minority. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

breakdown.why: The Interior Ministry's 2025 statistical review gives, for sexual abuse of a child under 15 (Art. 158), 313 victims of whom 8 were foreign citizens and 129 perpetrators of whom 11 were foreigners. DZS convictions by citizenship: 121 adults convicted of child sexual abuse and exploitation, 9 with other citizenship. Croatian/foreign citizenship only. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Violation of a child's rights (Art. 177, abuse and neglect by carers): 3,190 victims (2,132 under 14), 70 foreign; 848 perpetrators, 37 foreigners. Domestic violence (Art. 179a): 2,600 victims (55 children), 88 foreign. Foreign victims are not split by age. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Murder and aggravated murder: 103 victims (13 foreign; 5 under 14) and 97 perpetrators (13 foreigners) in 2025. Child victims are not split by citizenship. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Trafficking in human beings (Art. 106): 21 victims (3 aged 14-17; 12 foreign citizens of all ages) and 22 perpetrators (8 foreigners) in 2025. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Exploiting children for pornography (Art. 163): 275 child victims, 12 foreign; 176 perpetrators, 24 foreigners. Grooming (Art. 161): 16 victims. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Croatia scores 10% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. The Interior Ministry publishes victims and perpetrators of each offence, including child sexual abuse and child pornography, with a count of foreign citizens, and DZS publishes convictions by citizenship. That is a citizenship proxy only; no ethnicity is recorded.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
